title: Bounded-below derived proper base change
statement:
For a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f$ proper and
every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ with torsion cohomology,

$$
 \Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}K
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$.

proof.text: **Step 1 (unit step 1: $\mathbf P^1$).** For every scheme $S$ the projection $\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ satisfies $\mathrm{PBC}$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-property]: this is [prop-weil-pbc-projective-line] (Stacks 095T, proof, paragraphs 2-5: the strictly henselian comparison $H^q(\mathbf P^1_A,F)=H^q(\mathbf P^1_s,F|)$, the stalk formula, and the invariance of the cohomology of $\mathbf P^1$ under extension of separably closed fields, giving $\mathrm{IA}$ for the projection, which is then converted into $\mathrm{PBC}$). (The Lean of this step rests on two statements the Lean split off, [lem-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-bounded-below] and [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-flat-separator]; they are cited where the Lean uses them, in the proof of [prop-weil-pbc-projective-line].)

**Step 2 (unit step 2: the reduction).** By Step 1 the hypothesis of [prop-weil-pbc-reduction-to-projective-line] holds, so every proper morphism of schemes satisfies $\mathrm{PBC}$ (Stacks 0A4F: affine base, Chow's lemma, closed immersions are finite, $\mathbf P^1$ gives $\mathbf P^n$ through the finite surjective symmetric-product map, composition and cancellation along proper surjections). In particular, for every prime $r$, every proper $f$, every cartesian square and every sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ (a torsion sheaf, being killed by $r$), the exchange morphism $g^{-1}Rf_*F\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}F$ is an isomorphism: this is [lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change].

source.place: Theorem 095T (line 18610), proof, paragraph 1, and Lemma 0A4F (lemma-reduce-to-P1, line 18539)

proof.text: **Step 3 (unit step 3: finite torsion, then all torsion).** For every proper $f$, every cartesian square and every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$, the maps $g^{-1}R^pf_*F\to R^pf'_*g'^{-1}F$ induced by $\Ex_{\square,F}$ are isomorphisms for all $p$, i.e. $\Ex_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$: this is [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-assembly], obtained from the prime case of Step 2 as in the proof of Stacks 0A4B: if $nF=0$ and $n=rn'$ with $r$ prime, the sequence $0\to F[r]\to F\to F/F[r]\to0$ has an $\mathbf F_r$-sheaf on the left and a sheaf killed by $n'$ on the right, the exchange maps form a morphism between the long exact sequences of higher direct images, and the five lemma gives the case $F$ by induction on the number of prime factors of $n$; a general torsion $F$ is the filtered colimit of the $F[n]$, $g^{-1}$ and $g'^{-1}$ commute with colimits, and $R^pf_*$, $R^pf'_*$ commute with filtered colimits (Stacks 09Z1, $f$ and $f'$ being quasi-compact and quasi-separated). This is the statement of the unit.

**Step 4 (the two spectral sequences and their morphism).** Let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ have torsion cohomology and choose $a$ with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. The canonical truncation triangles $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to$ give, after applying the triangulated functors $g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $Rf'_*g'^{-1}$, two exact couples and spectral sequences [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations]
$$E_2^{p,q}=g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\Rightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(g^{-1}Rf_*K),\qquad E_2'^{p,q}=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)\Rightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$$
(the first is $g^{-1}$, which is exact, applied to the spectral sequence of $Rf_*$; the second uses $\mathcal H^q(g'^{-1}K)=g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$). The exchange morphisms on the three terms of each truncation triangle form a morphism of these exact couples [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples], which induces a morphism of spectral sequences compatible with all differentials and whose $E_2$-component in bidegree $(p,q)$ is the degree-$p$ exchange map $g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\to R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ of the sheaf $\mathcal H^q(K)$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-couple-differential]. Each $\mathcal H^q(K)$ is a torsion sheaf, so by Step 3 the morphism is an isomorphism on $E_2$.

source.place: Lemma 0DDE (lemma-proper-base-change, line 18708), proof (the spectral sequences E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*H^q(E), E'_2^{p,q}=R^pf'_*(g')^{-1}H^q(E); 'some details omitted', written out here with truncation couples)

proof.text: **Step 5 (all pages, convergence).** A morphism of spectral sequences that is an isomorphism on $E_2$ is an isomorphism on every page $E_r$, $2\le r\le\infty$ [lem-sp-page-induction]: $E_{r+1}$ is the cohomology of $(E_r,d_r)$ and the morphism commutes with $d_r$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence] both spectral sequences lie in $p\ge0$, $q\ge a$, so in total degree $n$ only $a\le q\le n$ occurs, every entry stabilizes after finitely many pages, and the induced filtrations of the abutments $\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)$ and $\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$ are finite, exhaustive and separated with $E_\infty$ as associated graded. Hence the morphism is an isomorphism on the associated graded objects of these filtrations.

**Step 6 (the abutment map).** By [lemma-weil-pbc-exact-couple-abutment] the map induced on the abutments in total degree $n$ is $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K}):g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)\to\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$; it respects the two finite filtrations and induces on the graded pieces the $E_\infty$-map, an isomorphism by Step 5. A morphism of finitely filtered objects inducing isomorphisms on all graded pieces is an isomorphism [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction], so $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})$ is an isomorphism for every $n$.

**Step 7 (conclusion).** A morphism of $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$ inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology]. By Step 6, $\Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$ is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$.

Of the six open Lean declarations, four belong to existing nodes (reported), two got new nodes (lem-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-bounded-below, lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-flat-separator), cited in Step 1 where the Lean uses them.
